page: Microsoft Azure B2as_v2 is a burstable, entry-level general purpose virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is equipped with an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 burstable vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Vector processing supports standard AVX instructions, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is present via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

The virtual machine includes 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per thread. It provides no local temporary storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistence via Premium Storage support. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs included on this tier, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark evaluations highlight clear single-threaded burst capability alongside aggregate multi-threaded constraints typical of shared, single-core burstable allocations. The instance achieves a strong stress-ng single-core score of 2,701.19 (top 25%), while its multi-core stress-ng metric remains identical at 2,701.19, placing it in the bottom 25%. Geekbench records 1,469.0 in single-core testing (middle 50%) and 1,813.0 in multi-core (bottom 10%). Memory bandwidth tests exhibit lower throughput, scoring 37.06 GB/sec for large read blocks and 24.89 GB/sec for large write operations. Practical workload synthetic tests reflect these constraints, generating 2.27 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 2.79 GB/sec.

Because the server couples burstable scheduling with low raw core count, it offers a cost-effective footprint for workloads with intermittent CPU activity. Workload fits include low-traffic web servers, development environments, staging microservices, small background automation tasks, and entry-level CI/CD runner jobs. Continuous high-throughput compute, heavy parallel compiling, and intensive relational databases are bounded by the underlying single physical core and shared burst model.
description: Microsoft Azure B2as_v2 is a burstable general purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs pinned across a single physical core with multithreading, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage, depending on remote storage solutions, and includes no discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate solid single-thread performance, posting a strong stress-ng single-core result of 2,701.19 and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1,469.0. However, multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall into the lower tiers due to core constraints and burstable resource limits. This profile makes B2as_v2 cost-effective for non-continuous, low-utilization tasks such as light web serving, development servers, code repositories, and entry-level automation.
